verdict.rationale: skills.sh is a registry and CLI that installs SKILL.md packages into other coding agents. It is not itself an agent or runtime that consumes tools, so being an MCP client that plugs in servers to use their tools is outside its product role. Nothing in the evidence shows the CLI connecting to MCP servers. The spec's experimental `allowed-tools` field describes tools the host agent may use, and the community Nix comment describes a different product managing MCPs, so neither makes this axis apply.
